Where the tree stands
I reconstructed the tree from dump.txt and verified SHA-256 per file: 389 of 390 verified. Two non-verifications, neither drift:

LICENSE — elided by export.sh by design (metadata + SHA only).
export.sh — its own content contains # FILE: separator text inside a heredoc, which truncates any splitter keyed on those headers. Not a defect in the dump; just unsplittable by that key.
tests/MyRestaurant.WebApplication.Tests/Time/RestaurantTimeTests.cs initially mismatched because it is the last file and my splitter swallowed the dump's trailing summary block; corrected and verified.

No drift between session memory and the tree. Post-Slice-72, spec v1.57, findings floor F-127, claude-terminal.txt shows 1332/1332 passing, all nine local CI gates green, 21/21 E2E, no outdated or vulnerable packages.

I emulated the §16.4 counted-class census against the reconstructed tree: 49 counted paragraphs, zero disagreeing with their files. Markdown, version-header and byte-hygiene checks are consistent.

What I found for the next slice
docs/MENU_AND_HANDHELD_PLAN.md is fully closed, so there is no named next row. The strongest open gap I located is this:

§11.12 is titled the handheld layout contract (every surface, every screen), and the §16.3 barrier reaches two surface families out of five. HandheldSurface declares exactly Administration (scenario 16, ten §11.4 pages) and GuestOrder (scenario 21, §11.1). /kitchen and /counter — the two stations R§1 justifies the whole contract with, the ones where somebody is standing up — have never been laid out at 375px by anything in this repository. That is the same species as F-118 and F-127, one register up: a floor reaches the subjects a barrier names, and a whole surface outside them is unmeasured.

Reading ahead on feasibility, the ground is favourable:

RestaurantInstance.OpenIsolatedPageAsync already takes handheld: true, and scenario 10 already opens an isolated counter page and signs a counter member in by password. Making that one page handheld costs one argument and touches neither the administrator's page nor the guest's.
Every control on both counter surfaces resolves to .link-button, .button-primary/.button-secondary or .form-field input/select, all of which carry min-height: var(--touch-target) and font-size: max(1rem, 1em) over an unstyled 16px body — the same declarations already proven green on §11.4 and §11.1.
Both counter components and KitchenBoard are flex-wrap throughout, with no media query anywhere outside app.css's single 48rem block, so sideways overflow is unlikely.
The kitchen is the harder half: KitchenJourneys.OpenAsync runs on the administrator's wide page, so measuring it needs a kitchen staff account and a second password sign-in — a duplicate of the counter's arrangement rather than a ride on an existing one.

What I'd propose
Slice 73 — the barrier reaches §11.3. Two new HandheldSurface records (CounterBoard, CounterSitting), scenario 10's counter page opened handheld, the board measured by navigation while the sitting is open, the bill measured where it stands just before BeginCloseAsync. New finding F-128 for the unmeasured-surface gap, with the kitchen recorded as a named deferral under §18's deferral rule rather than left implicit. Spec §11.12, §16.3 scenario 10, §16.4, Appendix A, changelog to v1.58; ledger row; BUILD_PROGRESS.md narrative; _CHANGES.md.

Predicted test count: 1332 unchanged — scenario 10 is one [Fact] before and after, and the new surfaces carry no attributes.
